newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Samper drug corruption trial may be reopened.
newsitem.headline: Samper drug corruption trial may be reopened.

text.p: Colombian President Ernesto Samper, cleared of wrongdoing in connection with his 1994 election campaign, may be subjected to another drug corruption probe in Congress, judicial officials said on Wednesday.

They said an appeal filed with the country's highest court by former Justice Minister Enrique Parejo, an outspoken Samper critic, could force Congress to reopen its investigation of charges that the president received millions of dollars from the Cali drug cartel to finance his scandal-plagued campaign.

The appeal before the Constitutional Court stems from the fact that Parejo was denied the right to participate in the probe, which was initially handled by the Committee of Accusations of the House of Representatives. He had demanded to participate as an ad hoc "people's representative" or ombudsman but his request was dismissed out of hand by the head of the congressional panel, a Samper ally.

Constitutional Court Judge Vladimiro Naranjo ruled on Tuesday that the denial of Parejo's request marked a violation of due process and justified the reopening of Samper's trial at the earliest possible date.

Carlos Gaviria, president of the Constitutional Court, said in a radio interview that all nine court justices would debate Naranjo's finding on Wednesday and rule on the possible reopening of the Samper case as quickly as possible.

The House of Representatives voted by an overwhelming 111-49 on June 14 to close the case that might have led to Samper's impeachment in the Senate, citing a lack of evidence to prove any wrongdoing by the embattled head of state.
Critics, including senior U.S. State Department officials, dismissed the decision as a whitewash.
